# ezghcloud_kubernetes_addon (Resource)

A managed add-on in a cluster. Add-ons a new cluster installs (vpc-cni, kube-proxy, coredns, pod-identity-agent, blockstore-csi) are taken over when declared, and left installed on destroy if they can't be removed. Fields EZGH manages are overwritten if changed in the cluster.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster (kcl_). Changing it replaces the add-on.
- `name` (String) Add-on name, such as coredns, files-csi, secrets-store, obs-agent or metrics-server. Changing it replaces the add-on.
- `project_id` (String) The cluster's project. Changing it replaces the add-on.

### Optional

- `configuration` (String) The add-on's configuration, a JSON object checked against its version's schema. Compared as JSON, so formatting isn't drift. Left out, none.
- `operation_timeout` (String) Maximum wait for each asynchronous operation, for example 10m.
- `version` (String) Pin the add-on to this version. Left out, it follows the cluster: each cluster upgrade moves it to the newest version for the new Kubernetes version.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Add-on ID (kad_).
- `installed_version` (String) The version the cluster runs.
- `operation_id` (String) Most recent operation initiated by this resource; unavailable on import.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization managed by the configured provider.
- `resource_name` (String) IAM resource name.
- `status` (String) What the add-on is doing: creating, active, updating, deleting or failed.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Replace identifiers with values from your organization.
terraform import ezghcloud_kubernetes_addon.example 'ORGANIZATION_ID/PROJECT_ID/CLUSTER_ID/RESOURCE_ID'
```
